 HomeSmart is seeking a hands-on applied AI engineer to work directly with internal teams and affiliated businesses. You’ll identify meaningful business problems and build practical solutions—from initial prototype through production and ongoing improvement. Some projects will have a clear scope; others will require you to investigate workflows and define the problem.
 This individual-contributor role partners with engineering, data science, and infrastructure teams. We welcome data scientists, applied AI/ML engineers, and full-stack developers with strong engineering skills; prior Forward Deployed Engineer experience is not required.
 What You’ll Do 
 Work with business teams to understand workflows, identify opportunities, and define success measures.
 Build and deploy production-ready applications, APIs, integrations, AI-enabled workflows, and automation.
 Develop reliable data pipelines and shared data models, including a business data ontology connecting people, activities, documents, and relationships across systems.
 Collaborate on machine learning architecture, training and inference pipelines, testing, and evaluation; troubleshoot issues and improve performance.
 Choose the right approach for each problem—AI/ML, deterministic logic, or conventional software—based on accuracy, latency, cost, and control.
 Build in security, access controls, traceability, error handling, testing, and human review; protect sensitive data and credentials.
 Monitor adoption, quality, time savings, and operating costs, then improve and maintain solutions after launch.
 What You’ll Bring 
 Experience building software or AI applications, with the ability to explain your contributions and technical tradeoffs.
 Strong Python skills; working knowledge of SQL, APIs, software engineering fundamentals, version control, code review, and testing.
 Experience building with language models and evaluating their capabilities, limitations, and production performance.
 Comfort using AI development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor—and the ability to debug, validate, and improve generated code.
 Sound security judgment around permissions, data integrity, sensitive information, and production credentials.
 Clear communication, curiosity, initiative, and the ability to work through ambiguity with technical and nontechnical partners.
 Helpful Experience 
 Experience with large-scale data systems, cloud infrastructure, deployment automation, machine learning, AI agents, retrieval, document understanding, workflow systems, semantic models, or ontologies is helpful. LangChain, LangGraph, and other orchestration tools are welcome.
 You do not need expertise in every area, a specific degree, or a set number of years of experience. We value demonstrated ability, sound judgment, and a willingness to learn. Professional work, independent projects, open source, and self-built products all count.
 What to expect in the interview 
 Be prepared to provide examples of your work such as a GitHub profile, portfolio, or project links. Public code is not required. Please do not share confidential or proprietary information.
 Why HomeSmart 
 Help shape how a real estate business operates. You’ll work closely with users, stakeholders, and experienced technical colleagues, with the opportunity to build solutions that improve individual workflows and become shared capabilities across the organization. Our hybrid approach combines collaboration in Scottsdale with focused engineering time.
 HomeSmart is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome qualified applicants from all backgrounds and evaluate candidates based on skills, demonstrated capabilities, and potential. Please let our recruiting team know if you need an accommodation during the hiring process.

Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform.
 The Role
 You own the marketplace surfaces where that decision happens — listing and submission, the offer moment, bidding and auction close, payout, the places where Alt asserts a price and asks someone to act on it. Design at Alt isn't a service function that receives requirements. It's the discipline that writes them.
 The bar you're held to: every surface you own ships with a written problem frame, a metric instrumented before launch, a readout you ran yourself — and craft good enough that a user screenshots it and sends it to someone. One without the other doesn't count here. A beautiful screen that didn't move anything is a miss. A number that moved on a surface nobody wants to look at is a different kind of miss.
 What You'll Own:
 The problem. You write the framing for your surfaces: who's hurting, the evidence, the number that says it's real, the metric that says it worked. AI-assisted, design-reviewed, never skipped. If nobody can state the problem in a sentence, it isn't ready to be solved.
 The craft. How completely the solution solves the problem, all the way to delight. It runs the full arc: reading the problem so precisely that the solution feels obvious in hindsight, shaping the flow so the user never has to think about the tool. It takes a user from "this worked" to "I want to show someone." That's still made by a person with taste and reps. We can generate a hundred options in an hour; you're here because you can make one of them solve the problem so well it delights.
 The solution space. Multiple real directions, converged against your surface's written bar. You'll pressure-test, extend, and validate with users — not pick the first thing that renders.
 The experience decisions. When a thing appears, what it feels like in the user's actual state, what tone it takes, what gets removed to make room, and what it does to neighboring screens. On a platform where people wire five figures based on what a screen makes them feel, these decisions are the product.
 The words. Copy is design here. The sentence that explains why an offer is what it is does more work than the layout around it. You write it.
 Trust, specifically. How much confidence we assert, when we show uncertainty, what the platform states versus suggests. As more of what we show a user is model-generated, this becomes the highest-stakes surface in the company, and Design has sign-off on it.
 The crafted base. The quality foundation your team iterates on, and its survival through implementation. You pair with engineers at ship time; built-versus-designed fidelity is yours.
 Your metrics. Instrumented before launch. You run your own readouts and kill your own misses.
 The research. Customer conversations every week, CX tickets and session replays mined as a habit, lightweight tests run by you, at the pace of the work. Your frames cite evidence because you went and got it.
 The prototype. You build. Working prototypes in code, not click-throughs, are how ideas get evaluated here, because a thing you can touch settles an argument in an afternoon that a doc would run for two weeks.
 How You'll Use AI Here:
 We don't want to hear that you use Claude every day. Everyone does. We want to know what you've built with it. Concretely, in this role:
 Get to a clickable prototype of a new flow in a day — real card data, simulated model output, testable interactions — so the team argues about a real thing instead of a doc
 Write a Claude skill that holds your surface's written bar , so every frame gets checked against it before it reaches review, and the bar stops depending on who's in the room
 Mine CX tickets and session replays at volume to find the pattern you'd never catch by hand — the phrasing that precedes an abandoned submission, the screen people revisit three times before they bail
 Turn a customer call into a synthesis the team can act on the same afternoon , not a deck three weeks later
 Generate and kill twenty directions before you commit to one, and be able to say what each one taught you
 Put a prototype in front of actual high-value sellers and come to roadmap planning with behavioral data — "version B moved stated acceptance likelihood, here's the prototype, here's the number"
 And have a view on the other side of it: where AI output is actively wrong for this work, and what you refuse to hand to a model. We ask.
 If you've built agents, written skills or MCP servers, wired up connectors, or shipped internal tooling your team actually depends on — lead with that. Name the artifact, not the tool.
 What You Bring:
 Relentless curiosity about users. This is the first bar. Not "I read the research" — you go and get it.
 You've made ambiguity tractable, more than once. Not a UI problem with a brief attached: a genuinely open problem, where you had to decide what the problem even was before anyone could work on it. You can tell us how you structured the chaos, what you chose not to solve, and how you knew when you had clarity.
 Articulation as part of your craft. You can state a problem so cleanly that the room aligns before a single mock exists, and defend a trade-off to an engineer, a founder, and a customer in their own languages. If we ask "what were you actually solving?" about your best work, the answer arrives in one sentence, not a walkthrough.
 Influence without authority. You've changed what a company built through the quality of your reasoning: reframed a roadmap, killed a bad direction, gotten engineers to fight for your design's details.
 Founding, first, or early designer experience — or you've built something of your own. You know what it costs to own an outcome end to end.
 You've shipped things you conceived , not just executed from someone else's spec, and you can narrate the problem-framing behind your best work unprompted.
 A portfolio organized around problems and outcomes, not screens. You talk about your work quantitatively: what moved, what you killed, what you learned.
 You prototype in code, or in code-adjacent tools, as a thinking medium. AI is already how you work. You can name the last thing you built with Claude, Cursor, Lovable, v0, or Figma Make — and what it got wrong. We'll ask you to show us, so bring something real.
 Bonus: marketplace or two-sided experience; high-consideration or financial products where trust was the conversion problem; consumer products with a passionate community; you collect, or you have a view on where this market is going.
 How We'll Interview You
 We'll be specific so you can prepare. Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, or sell. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go. For this role, pay attention to the submission, offer, and auction surfaces — those are the ones you'd own.
 1. Recruiter screen — 30 minutes The surfaces you own today and the metric you move. Why Alt. How AI actually shows up in your workflow. We'll answer your questions and talk comp.
 2. Hiring manager with Vijay, Head of Design — 60 minutes How you frame problems. Bring an open problem you had to define before anyone could work on it, and be ready on what you chose not to solve. Two or three pieces organized around problems and outcomes, not screens. Bring the numbers: what moved, what you killed, what you learned. We'll push back on at least one decision on purpose.
 3. Leore, our founder and CEO — 45 minutes. Everyone who joins Alt meets Leore, and he's in design loops daily, so this is a working conversation. Bring a point of view on a marketplace surface you'd go after first and why.
 4. Reference check(s) — 15 minutes with a former manager(s)

 We cover 85% of your medical, dental, and vision, and up to 50% for dependents. HSA/FSA available 
 Generous PTO that people actually take
 Parental leave at full salary
 $200/month wellness + $100/month home office stipend
 Free DoorDash Pass membership, because dinner shouldn't be a decision

ABOUT ARTERA 
 Our Mission: Make healthcare #1 in customer service. 
 What We Deliver: Artera is an agentic company strengthening how healthcare providers communicate and care for patients. As an agentic partner, we bring over a decade of healthcare experience to address urgent workflows from day one and build custom solutions as healthcare providers’ needs evolve. Trusted by 1,000+ specialties, FQHCs, health systems, and federal agencies, Artera strengthens and protects and enhances patient relationships across every interaction - from intake and scheduling to referral management, post-visit care, and more.
 Hear from our CEO , Guillaume de Zwirek, about why we are standing at the edge of the biggest technological shift in healthcare’s history! 
 Our award-winning culture: Our award-winning culture: Since founding in 2015, Artera has consistently been recognized for its innovative technology, business growth, and named a top place to work. Examples of these accolades include: Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024); Deloitte Technology Fast 500 (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025); Built In Best Companies to Work For (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026). Artera has also been recognized by Forbes as one of “America’s Best Startup Employers,” Newsweek as one of the “World’s Best Digital Health Companies,” and named one of the top “44 Startups to Bet your Career on in 2024” by Business Insider. 
 Applicants must be currently authorized and have the ability to provide proof of full-time, long-term authorization to work in the United States. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or support visa transfers now or in the future. 
 ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY 
 Artera is hiring an Associate AI Builder to build the agentic systems that deliver exceptional patient experiences for our customers — scheduling, referral coordination, medication refills, billing, payment estimation and more. 
 You'll be a contributing builder inside a customer-facing squad bringing AI-native fluency in delivering end-to-end on your customers’ needs — owning initiatives from customer discovery through production operation, onboarding new customers onto what you build, and shipping enhancements that keep pace with the technical possibilities for a named subset of our provider customers. Your creativity should be boundless, your desire to deliver world class solutions unmatched, and your initiative and accountability to those outcomes as a new bar for our customers they themselves aspire to. 
 At this level, you'll support/own customer outcomes independently with supervision, bringing the curiosity of a product manager, the discipline of a project manager, and the agentic fluency of an engineer to your work. You'll develop real subject-matter expertise and long term relationships with senior healthcare executives, and internally teach and support newer builders and experiment and advocate for novel agentic techniques that make every Artera customer even more successful. 
 This role supports a federal-facing product and is considered essential to secure operations. Candidates must meet eligibility for a government background check and comply with organizational security policies and federal data protection standards. The position includes responsibilities related to secure access, incident response, and operational continuity. Ongoing training and adherence to compliance requirements will be required.
 OUR APPROACH TO WORK LOCATION 
 At Artera, we believe the best work happens when people are truly connected. Our AI services model has shown what’s possible when small, focused teams move fast together — the speed of collaboration, pace of career growth, and quality of what we build can become stronger when teams share space. As we grow, we want every new teammate to feel part of an in-person community from day one.
 That’s why we are focusing our U.S. hiring in three cities, where we are investing in offices and building strong local teams:
 Santa Barbara, CA (Our HQ)
 Seattle, WA
 Kansas City, KS/MO
 Unless a role’s posting states otherwise, new U.S. roles are based in one of these three cities, and candidates should reside in (or be willing to relocate to) one of these areas. Each location follows an in-person schedule that reflects how our local teams work best; we’ll walk you through what to expect for your specific role and city during the interview process.
 Focusing on offices and hiring in a few locations, rather than spreading thin across many cities, lets us invest deeply in each one so every team has real community, mentorship, and momentum in person.
 WORKING AT ARTERA 
 Company benefits - Full health benefits (medical, dental, and vision), flexible spending accounts, company paid life insurance, company paid short-term & long-term disability, company equity, voluntary benefits, 401(k) and more! 
 Career development - Manager development resources, employee development funds 
 Generous time off - Company holidays, Winter & Summer break, and flexible time off 
 Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) - We believe that everyone should belong at their workplace. Our ERGs are available for identifying employees or allies to join. 
 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY (EEO) STATEMENT 
 Artera is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fair and equitable hiring practices. All hiring decisions at Artera are based on strategic business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications. All candidates are considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetics, protected veteran status, or any other protected status.

Artera provides reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees in compliance with state and federal laws. If you need an accommodation, please reach out to hr@artera.io.
 DATA PRIVACY 
 Artera values your privacy. By submitting your application, you consent to the processing of your personal information provided in conjunction with your application. For more information please refer to our Privacy Policy .

Those with specific security or privacy responsibilities must ensure compliance with organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and applicable standards and frameworks by implementing safeguards, monitoring for threats, reporting incidents, and addressing data handling risks or breaches.

 Ownership: Own end-to-end delivery and realized outcomes for named customers. Represent Artera credibly in customer conversations, and raise the bar on the customer solutions the squad ships.
 Strategy: Identify customer pain and create a roadmap for solving their problems.
 Program Management: Align stakeholders, connect necessary data pipelines, and manage fast and painless onboarding onto our solutions.
 Agentic Development: Build novel solutions for named customers; translate their operational reality into technical solutions that you yourself architect and code with our internal agentic systems.
 Continuous Improvement: Instrument, monitor, and improve the reliability of what you ship; create enhancements based on what production actually tells you; participate in on-call where applicable.

About Ramp 
 Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
 The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
 We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
 The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
 If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.
 About the Role 
 As a Design Engineer at Ramp, you sit at the intersection of design and front-end engineering. You bring ambitious ideas to life in real interfaces, prototype directly in code, validate with customers, and ship production experiences with a high bar for craft, performance, and reliability.
 Design at Ramp is AI first and builder led. Work starts in an LLM to clarify intent and constraints, moves into tools like Claude and Cursor to explore and build, is tested with real customers, and then comes into Figma for systems and polish. AI and self-serve research are default parts of the workflow, not side experiments.
 We are looking for multiple design engineers who think like a designer, code like a front-end engineer, and treat AI as a real collaborator.
 What You’ll Do 
 Design and build high-craft product experiences: Own key surfaces end to end, from concept through production. Use layout, interaction, and motion to make complex behavior feel simple and safe.
 Work AI first with Cursor and Claude Code: Use LLMs, Cursor, and Claude Code as your starting point. Draft intent, explore implementations, scaffold components, and refactor with AI in the loop. Apply your own judgment to refine quality.
 Prototype in code and validate with customers: Build interactive prototypes in React and TypeScript and test them with real users using self-serve research tools. Use what you learn to refine flows before full systemization.
 Bridge design systems, product, and brand: Translate Ramp’s design principles into reusable components and patterns. Extend the design system so expressive, brand-aligned moments are easy to build and scale.
 Reveal what our agents are doing without noise: Design patterns that show what AI and automation are doing on behalf of customers. Use hierarchy, copy, and motion to earn trust while keeping the default experience simple.
 Champion performance and accessibility: Ship work that is fast, accessible, and robust. Pay attention to semantics, focus states, reduced motion, and Core Web Vitals. Partner with engineers to debug and optimize over time.
